characters.name: Chicken
characters.description: The titular "Robot Chicken", although his name is only "Chicken" according toWord of God. As shown in the original credits, he was once a normal chicken that was run over by a car while trying tocrossa highway. However, he was found by theMad Scientist, who took him to his laboratory and turned him into aCyborgto bring himBack from the Dead, strap him to a chair and forced him to watchRobot Chickensketches. Advertised Extra: In the beginning, he was only present in the opening credits and had no presence or impact on the show itself, despite being the show's mascot and titular character. All for Nothing:Zig-Zaggedin regards to the rescue of his wife in "Fight Club Paradise". The Chicken fights his way back to the Mad Scientist's lab, only to be told that he made fried chicken of her. However, this is a lie and she is unharmed. Nevertheless, by the next special she has left him. Alternate Universe: In theStar Warsspecial, he plays the part of Darth Vader at the end ofRevenge of the Sith... before being forced to watch theStar Warssketches. Always Someone Better: After almost effortlesslymassacringthe Mad Scientist's minions through his castle, he finds himself completely outmatched in combat by theMad Scientist. In all likelihood, the Mad Scientist made him weaker than himself to avoid him turning the tables on him.

characters.name: Mad Scientist
characters.description: A psychotic, perpetually smilingMad Scientistthat lives in a dark castle. He turns the Chicken into a cyborg to revive him and make him watchRobot Chickensketches continuously. All There in the Manual: His real name is apparentlyFritzHuhnmörder, but he is known as the Mad Scientist.TheSaturday Night Liveopening parody has him as "Rick Sanchez". TheSaturday Night Liveopening parody has him as "Rick Sanchez". Alternate Universe: In theStar Warsspecial, he plays the part of the Emperor at the end ofRevenge of the Sith, using Force lightning to revive the Chicken. And I Must Scream: After being killed by the Chicken, he is revived and forced to watch TV in his place.

characters.name: Cluckerella
characters.description: The Chicken's wife, kidnapped by the Mad Scientist and forced to watch sketches in his place to lure him back. All for Nothing: Subverted in "Fight Club Paradise". The Mad Scientist tells the Chicken that he has made fried cuts out of her, but she's actually unharmed. Beauty Is Never Tarnished: The Mad Scientist doesn't mutilate her and add robotic body parts like he did to the Chicken, and only forces one of her eyes open instead of two. Bird People: A straighter example than her husband. Bizarre Sexual Dimorphism: She's a chicken but she has humanoid features like breasts and flowing blond hair.

characters.name: Mad Scientist's Son
characters.description: The Mad Scientist's twisted son, who steals his cyborg-making tools as part of a plot to kidnap all living US presidents for ransom. Amusing Injuries: He survives a free fall from a great height with no ill effects. Big Bad: Of the "Robot Chicken and Mad Scientist to the Rescue!" segment. Big Ol' Eyebrows: Has them despite being obviously younger than his dad. Presumably inherited them from him, and it was the Mad Scientist's eyebrows thatthinnedwith age. Call It Karma: After his defeat, the Mad Scientist straps him to the chair and forces him to watch sketches.

characters.name: Nerd
characters.description: A bucktoothed, bespectacled fanboy of all things geek. Aside from the titular Chicken, he is the show's most recurring character. Abhorrent Admirer:To hisCeleb CrushScarlett Johansson, and really, any female he takes interest in.In a non-romantic way, he's also this toGeorge LucasandGeorge R. R. Martin. To hisCeleb CrushScarlett Johansson, and really, any female he takes interest in. In a non-romantic way, he's also this toGeorge LucasandGeorge R. R. Martin. All Just a Dream: All his visits to established franchises can be counted as this, even when it is not explicitly stated. It also works well to discardNegative Continuityissues.He actually catches on from "The Nerd in Oz" and beginsaltering his dreamsto make themcooleror have aDream Within a Dreamthat is more to his liking.

characters.name: Humping Robot
characters.description: A non-talking iron humanoid robot that was introduced humping a washing machine in a sketch, either because he was programmed to or because he actually finds it arousing. It has since humped lots of different objects. Accidental Hero: His humping a clausured church's bell in "Humping Robot Saves Christmas" ends... doing pretty much that. Exact Words: In "Battlehump", the scientists theorize that "hump" must mean something different in the robots language because of their repeated announcement that they want to hump earthlings. However, they really meant humping. Giant Mook: In "Battlehump", several humping robots invade Earth including a giant one. Major Injury Underreaction: Gets to play the part ofthe one-armed soldierin aSaving Private Ryanspoof... except he humps his own severed arm.

characters.name: Aliens
characters.description: A race of wackygreyaliens that appear whenever the plot demands aliens not from an established franchise. Alien Abduction: They perform and alsofall victimto this. Alien Blood: They have green blood. All Just a Dream: "Smallville Crash Site" is actually a story told by Jonathan Kent to a youngSuperman. Anal Probing:Parodied in "Alien Abduction Reversal", where rednecks abduct an unsuspecting alien to probe his anusFor Science!. They also want him tosqueal like a little piggyduring the procedure.FurtherPlayed for Laughsin "A PR Nightmare", which reveals thatAnal Probingis something that happened only once but the Alienswill never be allowed to forget it. One alien explicitly says the usual procedure is non-invasive.

characters.name: Daniel a.k.a. "Gyro-Robo"
characters.description: Another nerd, this time more negative minded. He has an online show where he does nothing but complain about thingsRobot Chickensketches get wrong. Atrocious Alias: He credits insisting on "Gyro-Robo" as being why he is still a virgin. He even directly calls it causation, not correlation. Basement Dweller: Shown to spend too much time in his room, judging by the half eaten pizza and empty containers of soda and Chinese food. Bring Me My Brown Pants: Pisses himself when the Chicken gives him aDeath Glare. He's lucky that's all he got compared to most everyone else. Bulletproof Human Shield: Downplayed in theSaving Private Ryansketch, where he usesGreen and Senreich's bodiesas cover.

characters.name: Bloopers Host
characters.description: The mentally disturbed host ofBloopers!, anAmerica's Funniest Home Videos-style show. Big "NO!": In response to the incident inBy "No", I Mean "Yes". By "No", I Mean "Yes": While being held in a dungeon by a dictator, he is told that he'll soon be free. To watch his movies-on-demand service. Which only carriesChristmas with the Kranks. Comedic Sociopathy: TheBloopers!segments are overhelmingly violent and cruel, even by the show's standards. Cruel Mercy: In "The Rescue", he is surprised to be saved from committing suicide by hanging by the Chicken, only to have his head smashed in.

characters.name: Unicorn
characters.description: ADepraved Homosexualunicornfrom a magical land, always craving sex with a young malehuman. Absurdicorn: The unicorn is a recurring character and is shown to be a sexual predator who sexually harasses and coerces other characters into performing sexual favors for him. Ass Shove: He is forcefully shoved long objects up his ass twice. Of course he thinks not really bad about it. Bestiality Is Depraved: He is sexually depraved and he is only interested in having sex with humans. Breaking the Fourth Wall: In "The Lion, the Witch, and the Locker", he winks to the camera after saying that he'd like to "cross swords" with the Nerd.

characters.name: Gummy Bear
characters.description: An animated, sentient gummy bear that isdoomedto scream in painfrom stepping on a bear trap in every sketch she's in. Autocannibalism: In her first sketch, she cuts her trapped foot by eating her own flesh — which she notes, is delicious. Blood-Splattered Innocents: In theSaving Private Ryanshe spoofs, she gets almost completely covered in Lindsay Lohan's blood. Bulletproof Human Shield: Involuntary version in the aforementioned sketch, where Lindsay Lohan soaks up all the bullets, resulting in the Gummy Bear behind her being shocked but completely unharmed. Butt-Monkey: She just keeps getting stuck in bear traps.

characters.name: Munson
characters.description: A jerkish teenager that bullies the nerds, and specially Daniel. All Girls Want Bad Boys:Lindsay Lohancalls him one, and is instantly attracted to him. Bridal Carry: Carries Lohan like this after falling inLove at First Sightwith her. Dirty Coward:Seenrunning away screaming as soon as the Chicken comes near him in "The Rescue". Fourth-Date Marriage: Munson is shown living with Lohan and to have made her pregnant at the end of their sketch.

characters.name: Pablo Rodríguez
characters.description: AMexicanCyborgnicknamed "The Six Million Peso Man". The Artifact: His name and his cyborg nature are not referenced past his first episode. Cyborg: Like theThe Six Million Dollar Man, butMexican. Demoted to Extra: He is reduced to filling crowd scenes in his following episodes. Dynamic Entry: In "The Rescue", he manages to briefly get the drop on the Chicken when he's about to face off with three others via swinging kick and they gang up on him together, but it doesn't last long before the Chicken recovers andkicks all of them to the curb.

characters.name: Sunshine Cowboy
characters.description: A cowboy in summer vacation wear that is shot every time he appears on screen. Badass Bandolier: Two of them, over each shoulder. Boom, Headshot!: He appears in three sketches, in two he is shot through the head. Hoist by His Own Petard: The third time, he shoots himself with his own gun. Hope Spot: In "The Rescue", he sighs in relief when the Chicken walks past him... but is then shot by the Chicken.

characters.name: Composite Santa
characters.description: A bizarre, murderously insane individual, who is half-Santa Clauson one side and half-snowman on the other. Anachronism Stew: He was created from DNA samples inThe '50s, even though cloning from adult animals wasn't accomplished untilThe '90s. Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: In "A Very Dragon Ball Z Christmas", he steals Santa's sled, reindeer, and pants. Artificial Human: He was created in a laboratory by aMad Scientist. Ax-Crazy: The rare event is when he doesn't try to murder someone.

characters.name: Bitch Pudding
characters.description: A foulmouthed, crass denizen ofStrawberry Land. Alpha Bitch: "Bitch" isliterallyin her name. Pretty much speaks for itself. Alternate Universe: The later sketches put her in a completely different world without reference to Strawberry Land or any implication of it existing in the setting. For example, she replaces Abigail in a spoof ofThe Crucible, and plays aCowboy Copin aBuddy Cop Showparody titled "Murder, She Bitched". Anti-Heroine: She reluctantly becomes one for theSchlorpsin the "Bitch Pudding Special". Unfortunately, by that point nearly all Schlorps are dead. Repeats again in "Murder, She Bitched", which recasts her as a Cowboy Cop. The Artifact: Her name, a reference to her origin as a parodicStrawberry Shortcakecharacter, in sketches that make no reference to it.

characters.name: Citizens of Pastryville/Strawberry Land
characters.description: Extras usually appearing in skits that feature Strawberry Shortcake or Bitch Pudding. And There Was Much Rejoicing: In the "Bitch Pudding Special", the entire town of Pastryville celebrates with a giant festival when they think Bitch Pudding is dead. Ax-Crazy: Donotlet their cute looks fool you. They're happy to resort to murder in any situation. Beware the Nice Ones: For a bunch of cute, innocent-looking villagers, they can get pretty violent.In the "Bitch Pudding Special", the entire town attempts to murder Bitch Pudding after she gives a rude speech at Granny Grahamcrackers' funeral.Strawberry and her friends set the Purple Pieman's house on fire and stone him to death after accusing him of taking Black Cherry Pie's black cherry (as in, the fruit).explanation"Popping your black cherry" is a euphemism for losing your anal virginity.Strawberry has Huckleberry Pie arrested and hanged after accusing him of having sex with the Purple Pieman (actually, the Pieman was having sex withan actual huckleberry pieand yelled out its name in a moment of ecstasy). In the "Bitch Pudding Special", the entire town attempts to murder Bitch Pudding after she gives a rude speech at Granny Grahamcrackers' funeral.

characters.name: Gary the Stormtrooper
characters.description: A normal 29-year old husband and father of a young girl from Leeburg, Virginia who is employed as a Stormtrooper for the Empire ofStar Wars. Alternate Universe: Obviously, in theStar Warsfilms there isn't a young girl named Jessica accompanying her father Stormtrooper. Nor is it "bring your child to work" day at any point in the films. Ascended Extra: Literally and figuratively. The premise is that he is one of the millions of Stormtroopers in the first film, now shown as a main character. He also goes from starring in just one sketch in the secondStar Warsspecial to seven in the third special. Been There, Shaped History: He fought the rebels when they stole the Death Star's plans, was one of the patrolmen hypnotized by Obi-Wan, caused Luke's aunt and uncle's deaths, commanded the Death Star at one point and almost crashed it, survived its explosion by being aboard a TIE-Fighter, and walked in on Darth Vader throwing down the Emperor. Continuity Nod: When Beru tells him to stay until the droids return, he says "they are not the droids we are looking for, anyway".

characters.name: Little Drummer Boy
characters.description: Ananimesquedrummerlittle tin soldierspoof. Animesque: Because of his introduction during the "A Very Dragon Ball Z Christmas" sketch, he looks very similar to Goku and Gohan. Anti-Climax: His demons are destroyed by Goku as soon as they are summoned. The Artifact: However, later sketches make no mention to Manga and draw jokes only from his nature as drummer. He also doesn't use his drum to summon demons like in the original sketch. Ascended Extra/Demoted to Extra: Zig-Zagged. Introduced as a subordinate of Composite Santa, he appears in later sketches on his own capacity. However, all of these jokes are about the fact that he is a drummer boy, and not the supernatural Manga warrior he was introduced as.

characters.name: Mo-Larr
characters.description: A relentlessly dedicated dentist inEternia, who pulls rotten teeth out of hero and villain alike (but mostlySkeletor). Ambiguously Jewish: His real name is Moe Larrstein. Canon Immigrant: Mattel made an actual Mo-Larr figure in response to the skit that introduced him. Heroic Build: As befits any male born in Eternia. Mundane Made Awesome: "Mo-Larr: Eternian Dentist" retells his college education as if it was aSuperhero Originstory.

characters.name: Fumbles
characters.description: The Bad Guy Wins: Fumbles succeeds in wiping out all but one of the Joes, who he spares to make sure he lives with his decision of mistreating Fumbles that resulted in his friends' deaths... Butt-Monkey: He's this among G.I. Joe. Despite all his achievements and skills, the team bullies him because of a minor accident and treats him as nothing more than a janitor. This treatment leads directly towards his betrayal. Cold Sniper: He used to be theFriendly Sniperof the Joes but the Joes' cruel bullying turns him into a murderous killer and he kills his former comrades in humiliating ways. Combat Medic: He mentions that he's got a doctorate and can provide medical aid in the field if need be. Dark Is Not Evil: He once belonged to G.I. Joe and wears an all-black attire. That is until hisFace–Heel Turn.

characters.name: Negative Wonder Woman
characters.description: Dude Magnet: Yeah, there is little chance any man that isn't attracted to her.Wonder Woman:Don't grab her or anything.Superman:I grabbed her.Flash:Grab her until she couldn't walked. Innocent Fanservice Girl: Either that or she is too stupid to realize she is showing off her naughty bits in front of everybody. Large Ham: She's obnoxiously loud.Negative Wonder Woman:HEY WONDER WOMAN! FUCK YOU!

characters.name: Santa Claus
characters.description: The holidays' jolly bringer of toys. But a bit more jaded and dickish than usual. Accidental Pervert: He tries to hide from a little girl by going back into the chimney, only to get stuck halfway, and his pants to fall off... while wearingno underwear. Acrofatic: He has a big belly but also very defined muscles, impressive agility and strength. Adaptational Badass: This version of Santa isn't afraid to beat or shoot anyone. Adaptational Jerkass: ...nor to berate, hit, or kill his own employees, or to sleep with prostitutes, or to just take a gift from the sled to hide the fact that he forgot to make one for his wife.

characters.name: Martha Claus
characters.description: Santa's wife. And yes, she has a personality besides that. Adaptational Villainy: In "A Very Dragon Ball Z Christmas", where she isThe Man Behind the Manand turns into anEldritch Abomination. Awful Wedded Life: She is unhappy with her marriage, at least to a degree. Beware the Nice Ones: She's theThe Man Behind the Manin "A Very Dragon Ball Z Christmas", and can morph into aKaiju-esquemonster similar to the one inAKIRA. The Cobbler's Children Have No Shoes: She does not like Christmas, and is disappointed in being married to Santa Claus.

characters.name: Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer
characters.description: The red-nosed reindeer guide in Santa's sled. Adaptational Badass/External Retcon: In his first appearance, his red nose is revealed to be capable of shooting lasers at will. Animal Superheroes: He can fly, shoot lasers out of his nose, and leads the final fight against the monster Mrs. Claus. Eaten Alive: In "The Robot Chicken Christmas Special: The X-Mas United", he is eaten alive byzombieelves. Negative Continuity: He appears first as an average looking reindeer, then as the little one inRudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer(who is killed in one sketch).

characters.name: Comet
characters.description: An incredibly stupid reindeer in Santa's sled. Yet also successful. Crazy Enough to Work:Zig-Zagged. He throws himself into a well to rescue a trapped boy, claiming there is no time to wait for rescue services; as a result, he gets stuck in the middle. He suggests then to liberate him by throwing ahand grenadeinto the well and then another to get them both out of the well (nevermind that he can fly). The grenade kills a bunch of reindeer and destroys his legs, but succeeds in propelling him to the bottom of the well and the boy considers Comet his savior. Yet the rescue services are the ones who actually take both out of the well. Cloud Cuckoo Lander/The Ditz: Of Santa's reindeer, which are not much intelligent themselves. Leeroy Jenkins: He flies into the well despite Santa's objections, getting stuck. The other reindeer then follow on his advice to liberate him with a grenade, again ignoring Santa. Major Injury Underreaction: He doesn't mind losing his legs as he can fly, and doesn't seem to be in pain at all.

characters.name: Hermey the Elf
characters.description: The elf fromRudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer, who longs to leave Santa's workshop to become a dentist. Adaptation Dye-Job: Blonde in the original, Brunette inRobot Chicken. Oddly, the sketch features other blonde Elves. Crippling Overspecialization: The reason he fails at every endeavor he tries is because he knows nothing about anything but working at the North Pole for Christmas. Did You Just Punch Out Cthulhu?: He is introduced jumping on a giganticyetiand pulling out one of his fangs despite not being a dentist yet. Giftedly Bad: He fails at all of his endeavors, forcing him to return and beg Santa for his old job.

characters.name: Superman
characters.description: The Man of Steel... and kind of a douche. The Ace: Heissuperhuman, and he won't let people forget that, whether they have powers or (more often) don't. Adaptational Backstory Change: A mild variant. Everything else is the same, apart from Jonathan Kent having to get creative in disciplining him for misbehavior, and Krypton not actually being destroyed. Rather, Jor-El and Lara were going through a nasty divorce, and in a moment of spite, Jor-El blasted Clark off-planet with a rocket rather than give up custody of him. Adaptational Villainy: Though obviouslyPlayed for Laughsand witha softer sidethat surfaces from time to time, this egotistical version of Superman may be only third toCaptain HeroandHomelander. Alternate Universe: Most sketches are set in the classic comics and cartoons continuity or the 70s films, but some are in theMan of Steeluniverse.

characters.name: Batman
characters.description: The Dark Knight, an emotional basket-case. Actually Pretty Funny: He keeps his cool while Green Lantern laughs at theZoo Crew's appearance during Captain Carrot's funeral, but breaks down laughing when he hears Little Cheese's name. Adaptational Sexuality: Apparently bisexual inRobot Chicken, as he fantasizes both about having aPizza Boy Special Deliverywith Wonder Woman and wearing the veil while marrying Superman. Adaptational Villainy:As in the source material, Batman hasa rule not to killand stops one punch from killingThe Joker. But when pointed by Joker himself that he'll simplyescape from prisonand go back to commit crimes, he testifies against him to ensure he's given the death penalty and thenreplaces his wet sponge with a dry oneto ensure he has ahorribly painful death. Later on, he kills theHarmless VillainPalindrome just because he is irritated by his schtick of talking in sentences that are read the same forward and backwards.Another sketch has him (and Robin) as outright villains taunting and murdering children who dared sing "Batman Smells" during Christmas. However, this turns out to be a scary tale told by a music teacher so children will stop bastardizing "Jingle Bells". As in the source material, Batman hasa rule not to killand stops one punch from killingThe Joker. But when pointed by Joker himself that he'll simplyescape from prisonand go back to commit crimes, he testifies against him to ensure he's given the death penalty and thenreplaces his wet sponge with a dry oneto ensure he has ahorribly painful death. Later on, he kills theHarmless VillainPalindrome just because he is irritated by his schtick of talking in sentences that are read the same forward and backwards.

characters.name: Wonder Woman
characters.description: Amazon princess of Themysciraand the third most prominent member of the Justice League. Alternate Universe: In contrast to Batman and Superman, she generally keeps the look from the comics. However there is at least a promo forWonder Woman (2017)where she's modeled after it. Ambiguously Gay: In "The Real World: Metropolis", she tells Catwoman "who needs men, anyway" and to smile while caressing her leg. Maybe she was just being nice, maybe she wanted something more. Art Evolution: Her Season 1 model is an altered Barbie doll. Later seasons use a customized model. Designated Girl Fight:When the supervillains invade the Hall of Justice she's the one to fight Catwoman, Cheetah, and Harley Queen at once. However, she also fights Black Manta and the Penguin before and after.During the brawl at the beach before it is broken by Starro, she is full fighting Harley Queen, even though she's canonically superpowered unlike the latter.

characters.name: Aquaman
characters.description: A perpetually unlucky,wimpifiedversion of theSuperfriendsAquaman. Adaptational Wimp: In this show, he's a crybaby who can be neutralized by a secretary tripping him orslipping into a puddleon his own. Sea creatures are also just as likely to disobey him, or be useless in a fight. Alternate Universe: While he consistently has the same appearance and personality compared to most superheroes, there is one sketch that is based onAquaman (2018). Art Evolution: In "The Real World", he has black eyebrows and his shirt is plain without scales. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: The Justice League organizes an "Aquaman Appreciation Party" to show him that they actually like having him around. Unfortunately, he has already betrayed them to the Legion of Doom...

characters.name: The Flash
characters.description: The fastest man alive. Alternate Universe: Batman and Superman's breaking of the Multiverse causes the classic winged helmet version of Flash, Reverse-Flash, anda flasherto appear in the same place. Covert Pervert: He's okay with Kid Flash stealing Wonder Woman's clothingdespite pretending otherwise. Enemy Mine: Briefly puts aside differences with Reverse-Flash to fight Starro, but the Penguin accidentally incinerates both. Evil Counterpart: Reverse-Flash, a rather unimaginative example.Flash: Ugh, again with Reverse-Flash! He looks just like me, but with the exact opposite color scheme?Brilliant!

characters.name: Green Lantern
characters.description: Arch-Nemesis: Sinestro, who is also hisEvil Counterpartas he fights with another magic ring, just yellow. An Arm and a Leg: During a skit where he battles with Sinestro, his nemesis literally disarms him. Hal manages to keep being a Green Lantern by having his ring remade to fit around his penis. Comically Missing the Point: After Sinestro cuts off his arms and he gets a cock ring as a replacement, Flash asks why he couldn't just get a toe ring instead, to which Green Lantern replies, "Uh, how will a toe ring fit on my penis, stupid?" Pet the Dog: During aDecon-Recon Switchwhere he and Batman discuss how it's a bit demeaning if practical to bring the Caped Crusader into battle in one of his energy construct bubbles. They compromise by having Hal transport him in aCool Boatinstead.

characters.name: Green Arrow
characters.description: Attending Your Own Funeral: Batman goes on a rant at Green Arrow's funeral, claiming that mourning is pointless because superheroes always comeBack from the Deadsooner or later. By the end of his rant, Green Arrow is indeed alive, attending his own funeral, and applauding Batman's words. Driven to Suicide: In Batman's simulation, he commitsseppukuwith his own arrow after Batman cuts the string of his bow. Logical Weakness: Batman's plan to defeat Green Arrow in the event that he turns evil is to cut the string of his bow. Sidekick: Speedy, a horny, bratty teenager.

characters.name: Martian Manhunter
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: Hangs around in bars shapeshifted into an attractive woman, and when inquired about it he says he has a life out of the team. Attractive Bent-Gender: Because he can shapeshift at will. Kill It with Fire: Batman's plan to defeat him in the event of turning evil is to set him on fire. Robin is surprised that fire is his one weakness, to which Batman retorts...Batman:Fire is everyone's weakness. It is fucking fire. Little Green Men: Not so little but he's a green alien. Martians: The clue's in the name.

characters.name: Cyborg
characters.description: No Waterproofing in the Future: He electrocutes as soon as he steps in the ocean to fight Starro. Token Minority: Only black member of the Justice League.

characters.name: Doctor Fate
characters.description: Not That Kind of Doctor: One sketch has him go out on a date, only for things to go awry when a fellow diner starts choking and Dr. Fate has to awkwardly explain that his doctorate is not in medicine.

characters.name: Robin
characters.description: The Boy Wonder, Batman's wimpysidekick. Accidental Murder: In "3 Fast 3 Furious", he accidentally decapitates one of theCHiPsafter throwing an automatic grappling hook at them, which makes Robin panic and leads to the Batmobile being overturned and Robin run over by another racer. Amazingly, theCHiPcontinues the race headless and only falls over after being awarded for winning the race. Adaptational Villainy: In "Batman Smells", both he and Batman murder some carollers. Adaptational Wimp: InRobot Chicken, Robin issqueamish and weak. Batman's plan to subdue him in the event of turning evil is to slap him once. In theDC ComicsSpecial, he is seen exercising with a small dumbbell whilePower Girllifts a giant weight with only one arm next to him. Alternate Universe: A particularlyMind Screw-y sketch hasBurt Wardkidnapping the "real" Robin in order to use a Lazarus Pit to rejuvenate himself and revive the 1966Batmanshow.

characters.name: Speedy
characters.description: Green Arrow's sidekick. Adaptational Villainy/Teens Are Monsters: Launches a boxing glove arrow from orbit just to hit Kid Flash's mom, likely killing her.For the Lulz. Kid Flash beats him up for that one. Hormone-Addled Teenager: Introduced while tricking Wonder Woman in describing a handjob. Green Arrow slaps him for it. Non-Indicative Name: He's Green Arrow's sidekick, not Flash's. Sidekick: To Green Arrow.

characters.name: Lex Luthor
characters.description: Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: Canonically, Lena Luthor is Lex's sister, but she is his teenage daughter inRobot Chicken. Alternate Universe: In the "DC Comics Special III - Magical Friendship", Lex is visited by three alternate versions of himself; a Lex who still has his hair, is a rich hairdresser and not a criminal mastermind, a Lex wearing his warsuit andhas killed multiple Supermenand a Pez Dispenser Lex. Lex would gather them to form a new music band called Sexx II Men. Bad Boss: Lex is domineering and ill-tempered towards his group that he considers prison to be enough downtime for them. Bald of Evil: Well, he is Lex Luthor after all, complete with his iconic dome. '80s Hair: He was a glam rock ringer while in high school in the 80's, with accompanying mane.

characters.name: The Joker
characters.description: Alternate Universe: Usually has the cartoony appearance of early comics, but "Moral Quandary" and "You Can't Be Serious" parody theThe Dark Knightversion. Dung Fu: Fakes a prison escape to trick Batman into going into the sewers so he can unload into a toilet and flush the contents down the pipes and right onto his jailer. Heel–Faith Turn: In the sketch where he gets electrocuted, he claims that he knows Jesus has forgiven him. When asked if this is a joke, he sobs and replies "No". Joker Immunity: The comic cover of "The Death of the Joker" is followed by several issues of "The Return of the Joker", no doubt mocking him being theTrope Namer. Named by the Adaptation: The Joker's real name is ordinarily unknown, but the sketch where he gets sent to the electric chair gives his full name as Maurice P. Joker.

characters.name: Catwoman
characters.description: The Baby of the Bunch: the youngest contestant in "The Real World: Metropolis". Cat Girl: She can move her tail and uses "meow" to denote surprise. Gasshole: She can do some serious burping. Goofy Print Underwear: WearsHello Kittyunderwear, which Superman steals. Once Done, Never Forgotten: In "The Real World", she thinks she's not taken seriously because she got drunk and danced topless at a party.

characters.name: Two-Face
characters.description: Fatal Flaw: As in canon, his overreliance on his coin, to the point where he can't decide on what to order at the Hall of Doom's coffee shop or how to go to the bathroom without flipping it.

characters.name: Bane
characters.description: A luchador-esque supervillain with a fixation for breaking Batman's back. Alternate Universe: In most sketches he has the appearance ofThe '90s's comics and cartoons, but there is another set inThe Dark Knight Risesjust to make fun of the voice, and another where Batman and Bane are dogs (and Bane still breaks Batman's back). Refuge in Audacity: In his quest to break Batman's back again and again, he goes as far as walking into the Hall of Justice and doing it in front of every other superhero.They do nothingeven after Batman calls them out. Running Gag: Breaking Batman's back. Batman thinks he's off after three times, but he does it again (plus a fifth time as dogs). He also breaks his phone in the same way after failing to order a burrito.Batman: AaaahRule of Three, asshole! Not four! The Speechless: In most of his sketches, he simply walks in scene and breaks Batman's back without saying a word. "Bane vs Siri" has him speak purely to make fun of the voice.

characters.name: Cheetah
characters.description: Historical Rap Sheet: Apparently, Cheetah's responsible for the death of the real Princess Diana. She's shocked to learn it was the "wrong limo" (rather than her archenemyWonder Woman) and is last seen lamenting that she'd been "a candle in the wind".

characters.name: Scarecrow
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: The RC version of Scarecrow is a far cry from the fear-obsessed psychopath of the comics, being more sensitive and meek, is a caring uncle and lovesGilmore Girls. Black Comedy Rape: Scarecrow gets assaulted by an alligator when he tried to reclaim his shoe from swamp water. The fact that he knows the gator by name and asks him to "go gentle this time" implies this has happened on a regular basis. Butt-Monkey: Starting from theRobot Chicken DC Comics Special 2: Villains in Paradise, Scarecrow nearly gets burnt to death when trying to escape prison, gets raped by an alligator, have his laptop destroyed by Lex, gets mocked for his appearance, having to see Penguin's buttocks, Green Arrow stomping on his jewels, and gets burnt alive again. Cool Uncle: Scarecrow helps his nephew, Calvin to get a job at the Legion of Doom.

characters.name: Penguin
characters.description: Black Comedy Rape: After being thrown into a prison cell, the Humping Robot closes the door behind them and does the deed onto the Penguin. Distracted by the Sexy: Penguin is about to fight Robin only to be entranced by his smooth legs and gets kicked in the face by the Boy Wonder. Fan Disservice: He's an obese man with an unsightly appearance that seeing him in full nude would make your eyes melt. Just ask Scarecrow... Nasal Trauma: Gets his nose broken by Wonder Woman when he tries to persuade the superheroine to not hit his groin. Nice Job Fixing It, Villain!: Penguins tries using his umbrella's flamethrower against Starro only to lose control of it and burns alive many of his allies.

characters.name: The Riddler
characters.description: Start My Own: Riddler decides to form a new team when the Legion of Doom refuse to make riddle-based traps. He quickly regrets it when he realizes the Punctuation Posse is supremely lame.

characters.name: Sinestro
characters.description: Becoming the Mask: Sinestro initially took in Asian children to use their yellow skin to counter Green Lantern's power ring but comes to adore them like his own. My God, What Have I Done?: Sinestro is mortified when he accidentallylobs off Green Lantern's handsandflees the scene.

characters.name: Black Manta
characters.description: Actually Pretty Funny: Despite calling Joker insane for pulling a nasty prank on Batman, Manta still admits it is hella funny. The Narrator: He is this in the Arkham Redemption where he recounts Joker's time in Arkham Asylum. Screw This, I'm Outta Here: Black Manta bolts it out of the Legion of Doom after Giganta allows Aquaman to enter the base.

characters.name: Grodd
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: This Grodd is a far off take compared to how he is usually portrayed as a megalomaniacal tyrant. He treats his Legion of Doom members like fellow officer workers and a supportive friend towards Lena Luthor. Killer Gorilla: Mostlysubvertedthanks toAdaptational Heroism. He is overall a prettyNice Guydespite him helping supervillains in destroying the Justice League andTake Over the World. Ship Tease: He seemingly has feelings for Lena Luthor only to actually to have beenPlayed Withwhere it is Bizarro that the gorilla is in love for.

characters.name: Captain Cold
characters.description: Laser-Guided Karma: Captain Cold gets crushed to death by Starro for flushing the alien starfish into the toilet. Pungeon Master: He is prone to make a lot of ice-based puns. And it isn't unusual since Mr. Freeze, Icicle and Chillblaine do the same too.

characters.name: Bizarro
characters.description: OOC Is Serious Business: The fact Bizarro even covers his nose from Glen's body odor because it smellsTHATbad.

characters.name: Braniac
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: His typical comics portrayals have him being anOmnicidal Maniac; here though, he is a very polite person. He even acts as a supportive figure towards Scarecrow to taking off his mask. Breaking the Fourth Wall: He frequently breaks the fourth wall in the third special, although many of the characters are disturbed on what he is doing. I Warned You: He is ecstatic in being proven right that Starro would come back with a vengeance after Captain Cold flushed him down the toilet. Though, he gets crushed to death before he could brag it to Captain Cold who also dies alongside him.

characters.name: Lois Lane
characters.description: Superman'sLove Interestand fellow reporter at the Daily Planet. Bullying a Dragon: After marrying Superman, she annoys him constantly by demanding he fly back in time to remind her of playing her TIVO, only to act like he's insulting her intelligence and humiliating her in front of her friends because of that, then acting absurdly jealous. Clingy Jealous Girl: When Superman travels back in time to remind her to set her Tivo, she takes offense, accusing him of doing it for future Lois but not for her. Another time travel later, she's mad that Superman would travel back in time forTop Chefand not for her, without waiting for him to explain that he is doing it for her. Cruel and Unusual Death: This annoys Superman to the point that he goes back in time to let her die at the end of the 1978 movie, drowning in mud and screaming for someone to help her. Love Interest: To Superman. For decades without moving forward, as Green Lantern reminds him in "Out to score".

characters.name: Jonathan Kent
characters.description: Superman's adoptive father in Kansas. Abusive Parents: He couldn't punish child Clark physically so he damaged him psychologically by claiming that he was an accomplished space alien killer. All for Nothing: "No, Clark" shows Jonathan's death inMan of Steel, except it's a lot longer andmore humiliatingfor Jonathan, and Jonathan accidentally blurts out thatClark has superpowersbefore he dies, making it aSenseless Sacrifice. Alternate Universe: Most sketches are set in the 1970s films but "No, Clark" is set inMan of Steel. One-Man Army: "Smallville Crash Site" shows him slaughtering a crashed UFO's crew without getting a scratch, but this is clearly a lie.

characters.name: Martha Kent
characters.description: Superman’s adoptive mother in Kansas. Good Parents: She call outs Jonathan for making scaring stories to disipline Clark, then comforting her son after being informed the actual circumstances of him being blasted off Krypton.

characters.name: Jimmy Olsen
characters.description: Superman's best friend and also a reporter at the Daily Planet. Back from the Dead: He dies by falling out a window in "Villains in Paradise", only to be revived via magic amulet by the end. Covert Pervert: When he learns that Lois Lane died with "The Blowjob Network" on the TV, his mind immediately jumps to subscribing to it. Foil: He's pretty much Superman's Robin, except for not being a masked vigilante and being unaware of hisSecret Identity. As a result, he appears a lot less in the series.

characters.name: Luke Skywalker
characters.description: The Chosen Onewho will save the galaxy, who else? Adaptational Jerkass:Downplayed, but this Luke is clearly not as morally pristine as his movie counterpart. Among other things, he is a regular at theTosche Stationstrip club, sleeps withLeiaand grins when she says that it is wrong, andagreesto Vader's offer to rule together (but falls accidentally when he tries to join him). Big "NO!": Obviously, the one afterThe RevealinThe Empire Strikes Back, which is parodied in several sketches including "Luke learns the truth", the first to referenceStar Warsin the show. Demoted to Extra: Luke appears in many sketches, but they tend to be short physical gags or revolve around secondary characters promoted to main. Ooh, Me Accent's Slipping: A variant, in that watchers generally find Hamill to sound more likeThe Jokerthan Luke due to his age. Perhaps because of that, Hamill returned in other episodes to voice Joker but never again Luke, who fell to Bergen instead.

characters.name: Darth Vader
characters.description: The feared Dark Lord of the Sith. Who is still carrying a lot of baggage from his Jedi days. Adaptational Angst Downgrade: The torturedFallen Heroof the source material he is not. Best demonstrated in his first moments in the suit: in stark contrast to hisreactionin the film, the first thing he does once he's off the operating table is kick off adance partyto celebrate his recovery. Adaptational Nice Guy: He's still guilty of his canon crimeslike killing younglingsnotethough he went to hisImagine Spotfor thatand serving a dictatorship, but he's a lot more personable here and isn't as much of aBad Boss. Adaptational Wimp: Played with in "Death Star Orientation" as the Imperial officer giving the orientation reveals that his Force Choke ability isn't actually a thing. Officers on the receiving end of his wrath simplyfake being choked to deathand are given disguises afterwards. However theyonlydo it out of fear of Vader using his lightsaber instead if he ever figured it out. Affably Evil: He's generally a nice guy when not on the job, and the show changes him from aYou Have Failed MeBad Bossto aA Father to His MenBenevolent Boss.

characters.name: Emperor Palpatine
characters.description: The supreme leader of the Empire. Who is stuck dealing with all the little annoyances that entails. Adaptational Backstory Change: Though relatively the same as it still has him as a politician of noble upbringing who thought he could run the galaxy better than the current system, he became a Sith Lord on his own initiative. Adaptational Nice Guy: While still aJerkasshere, Palpatine isn't portrayed asthe psychopathhe is in canon. He's more a grumpy bosswho happens to be a galactic dictator. For example, his first appearance has him apologizing to Vader for bringing up Padme after yelling at him for the Death Star blowing up,noteAlthough he does motion a rude gesture afterwards.while canon Palpatine would at best not give a shit about how he'd feel. Breakout Character: Thanks to the famedphone call with Vader, RC Palpatine became a series standby. Even getting the third Star Wars special focused on him. Fantastic Racism: He refused to share an elevator with a bunch of Quarren because "I don't want to be smelling like a fucking filet-o-fish all day!"Quarren: ...That's hurtful, man.Palpatine: Then next time, just let it go! Let it go.

characters.name: Obi-Wan Kenobi
characters.description: Dirty Old Man: Jedi Mind Tricks himself in the mirror with the phrase "You have a lot to offer a woman." Heroic Comedic Sociopath: "Oh, the Jawas weren't dead, they were just stunned."Cue C-3PO reacting in horror that he had just burned several Jawas alive. Groin Attack: His idea of "training" Luke.

characters.name: Han Solo
characters.description: Cruel and Unusual Death: In Boba Fett’sImagine Spot, he takes a blind Han to Hoth and throws him to a pack of Tauntauns, which then draw-and-quarter him. "Fawlty Towers" Plot: "Slight Weapons Malfunction" expands the scene where this happens inA New Hopenotei.e. a guard hears shots through the Death Star's interphone, Han claims it was a "slight weapons malfunction" and radiation is leaking from a nearby reactor that the guard knows is not in that areaby having Han pick a name of a random from a employee's booklet, who gets contacted immediately and alsodoes not knowabout any reactor in the area. Then Han mentions Vader must have it installed yesterday, so the guard connects to Darth Vader but he doesn't know about a reactor either, then he calls his secretary to check the Death Star's plans, sees there's no reactor in the prisoner control room but decides to have one built, leading to the guard sending a team to install the new reactor. Han tells him they have it covered, shoots the communicator, before gettinghyped up to build the reactor. Sitcom Arch-Nemesis: With Boba Fett.

characters.name: Boba Fett
characters.description: The Best Bounty Hunter in the League. Breakout Character: Much like with Emperor Palpatine above, RC Boba Fett became a standout character in the Robot Chicken Star Wars episodes. Disappeared Dad: Much like in-canon, Boba’s father Jango Fett was killed by Mace Windu on Geonosis. Expy: RC Boba Fett is essentiallyDeadpoolinStar Wars. Merchandise-Driven: Emperor Palpatine gripes about how in Robot Chicken Star Wars Episode III that they were contractually-obligated to follow the story of Boba Fett.Palpatine: That's what you get for selling the most action figures. Thank you,fanboys!

characters.name: Yarael Poof
characters.description: Ascended Extra: Went from being a minor background character inPhantom Menaceto the subject of a trilogy of skits that give a comedic explanation as to why he's absent for the rest of the prequels. How the Mighty Have Fallen: Yarael used to be part of the Jedi Council before the Rise of the Empire had occurred and is now working as a cafeteria worker on the Death Star. No-Respect Guy: No one in the Jedi Council respects Yarael and only find him useful in bringing the pizza. Ironically, him getting the pizza saved him from Order 66. Oh, Crap!: Yarael is terrified when Palpatine and Darth Vader are next in line in the cafeteria. Paper-Thin Disguise: The only thing he uses to disguise himself is a moustache and no one notices.

characters.name: Jar Jar Binks
characters.description: Adaptational Badass: Surprisingly,yes!Jar Jar in canon did not have any Force abilities or manipulative skills. Bad People Abuse Animals: Implied to have killed several animals and mounts their heads on his wall. Evil All Along: Turns out he is a Sith Lord like Palpatine. Evil Laugh: Jar Jar, of all people, gives a bone-chilling laugh after finding the idea of Palpatine "manipulating" him hilarious. Eviler than Thou: Not only is he a presumed Sith Lord but it is also implied that Jar Jar allowed himself to be "manipulated" by Palpatine so that the Emperor would be a target for everyone, while leaving Jar Jar alone to carry out his own plans.

characters.name: Dengar
characters.description: Motor Mouth: Yeah, Dengar doesn't know when to shut up and people are actively trying to avoid him at all costs. Reliable Rustbucket: No joking, having a toilet-shaped ship is ridiculous but it does a good job at least in tracking the Millennium Falcon.

characters.name: He-Man
characters.description: Adaptational Jerkass: He threatens to rape Skeletor's skull right before Beast-Man kills him. Disproportionate Retribution: He, along with the other Masters, murdered frat boys for egging on Castle Grayskull. The Friend Nobody Likes: None of the Masters respect He-Man for beingThe Killjoyand ragging on their fun. Would Hit a Girl: He-Man displays no problems kicking Evil-Lyn right at the crotch.

characters.name: Orko
characters.description: Motive Decay: He took the Power Sword to avenge He-Man but when the Sorceress reveals that they can use the weapon to resurrect their friend, Orko kills her, so that he can have all the powers to himself. Roaring Rampage of Revenge: Orko takes the Power Sword to empower himself and kills Skeletor and Evil Warriors for murdering He-Man. Took a Level in Badass: He gets fucking ripped when he accesses He-Man's Power Sword and slaughters the Evil Warriors.

characters.name: Man-E-Faces
characters.description: Business Trip Adultery: In "The Many Faces of Man-E-Faces" reveals that the titular character has three families, each one relating to one of his personas. He ventures to them under the excuse of helping He-Man saving the world.

characters.name: King Randor
characters.description: Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: Rallies the other Masters to murder He-Man because they love the "new" He-Man. The Thing That Would Not Leave: Randor stays with his son at Castle Grayskull. It didn't take long before his constant annoyance drives He-Man to bring his father to a retirement home. Wouldn't Hurt a Child: He admonishes the people for brutalizing a infant Skeletor, only until he sees the baby's hideous mug and tries calling back the people to kill him.

characters.name: Skeletor
characters.description: Arch-enemy of He-Man. And just as incompetent as he ever was. Accidental Hero: In "Baby Want More", his scheme of getting spanked in baby form by a nanny because it turns him on accidentally ends up exposing her as abusive to the kingdom. Baby Morph Episode: He becomes a baby in "Baby Want More" to infiltrate Eternia's nursery and in "Skele-terminator" as a side effect of time-traveling to before He-Man was born. Bring Me My Brown Pants: Referenced in "The Death of He-Man" sketch;Orko:(muscle-bound and wielding the Sword of Power)I HAVE THE POWER!Skeletor: I have crapped my pants! Butt-Monkey: Nothing goes right for him like in his home series, and with this show's edgier adult humor, he tends to suffer much more, up to and including death.

characters.name: Beast-Man
characters.description: Barbaric Battleaxe: Carries around a battle axe which is able to cut into He-Man's spine, killing him. Climactic Maiming: Chews out his own arm to free himself from the boulder holding him in place. The Dragon: Seems to be Skeletor's second-in-command and is always roped into his boss's myriad of pathetic schemes. Hero Killer: The Death of He-Man is kickstarted when Beast-Man murders the titular hero. Hidden Depths: Beast-Man likes to watchRachael Ray.

characters.name: Evil-Lyn
characters.description: Hidden Depths: She likes to watchRachael Ray.

characters.name: Faker
characters.description: Always Someone Better: The clone is both smarter and stronger than He-Man. Not to mention that he is unanimously loved by the other Masters and the people of Eternia. Dumbass Has a Point: The Faker makes a good point that the Masters aren't even working out. Obfuscating Stupidity: After He-Man makes fun of his seemingHulk Speak, Faker drops the act and reveals he can speak eloquently and only plays the fool because he is playing in-character to the real He-Man. Turned Against Their Masters: He betrays Skeletor to continue partying.

characters.name: The Hulk
characters.description: Potty Failure: Hulk opts to pee on the sink rather than going to the bathroom. Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: Somehow, Hulk mistook a little boy to be Iron Man and does aFastball Specialon him against aKiller Robot.

characters.name: Falcon
characters.description: Token Minority: Being the only black person in the cast gets Falcon triggered whenever someone uses the word 'black'.

characters.name: Cobra Commander
characters.description: Bad Boss:ZigZagged. On one hand, he can be quite fair and congratulates his troops for doing a good job. Then again, he is also not above throwing his own subordinates to the wolves. And also not above shooting troopers so he'll have names on his Wall of Villains. Bullying the Dragon: Don't ever ruin Cobra Commander's roast; Just ask that undercover GI Joe operative who got shot in the head. Dirty Coward: Throws Baroness to take the bullets from the military. Even Evil Has Standards: The Commander is horrified when Carole Baskin admitted she had her cats to murder her husband. Green-Eyed Monster: After seeing GI Joe winning a PSA Award, he has COBRA make one of their own. It fails and in fact, G.I. Joe wins another award for making a PSA about COBRA's failed attempt.

characters.name: Duke
characters.description: Adaptational Jerkass: He is prone to putting those that he deems useless in humiliating situations. Cruel Mercy: Duke is intentionally left alive by Fumbles (aka. Trouser Snake) after killing the rest of the G.I. Joe forces so that he lives in anguish. Everyone Has Standards: Not even Duke likes the G.I. Joe Extreme team. A Father to His Men: He is shown to be a caring leader to the Joes (except Snow Job and Fumbles). Screams Like a Little Girl: The moment he realizes that the enemy is firing bullets and missiles, he shrieks like a harlot.

characters.name: Dora
characters.description: Adaptational Jerkass: She treats her friends like crap and occasionally tells the audience to screw off. Et Tu, Brute?: She does not take it well when Boots abandons her to the gorillas.Dora:Boots, you son of a bitch. Frame-Up: Swiper reports fake news that Dora is an illegal immigrant, causing her to be arrested and be forcibly deported out of the country. Pet the Dog: Dora tries to save Diego and screams in horror when he falls to his death.

characters.name: Boots
characters.description: Dirty Coward: Heavily implied to have abandoned Dora to the mercy of theKiller Gorillas. Killer Gorilla: Boots is an adorably monkey when younger, but unfortunately, when he got older, he becomes as blood thirsty as Travis the Chimpanzee. Neck Snap: What happens to Boots by Social Services under "CDC Regulations".

characters.name: Swiper
characters.description: All Men Are Perverts: Swiper loves to sexually harass on women, hence his other title, "The Virginity Swiper". Better to Die than Be Killed: Apparently, shooting himself is preferable than letting theGrim Reaperdo the deed. Karma Houdini: The only punishment Fox News does to Swiper for harassing one of his female co-workers is to terminate him...with a handsome bonus. Laser-Guided Karma: Swiper gets revenge on Dora for leaving him to freeze in the mountain's cold by stealing Diego's mountain equipment, causing his death. Then, Dora gets back at Swiper by offering him an empty gun to give him aHope Spotthat he can end his own life.

characters.name: Scooby Doo
characters.description: Ass Shove:Jason Vorheesshoves his machete right in Scooby's butthole. Dirty Coward: Scooby uses the time Jason is busy killing Shaggy to escape.Scooby Doo:Better Shaggy than me. Et Tu, Brute?: Scooby abandons Mystery Inc. to join theGhost Adventurescrew.

characters.name: Fred Jones
characters.description: Dirty Coward: Fred leaves Daphne to be killed byJason. Never Mess with Granny: Fred slapsPhyllis Dilleron the face after the latter makes fun of his ascot. Phyllis punches him in retaliation. No-Respect Guy: Fred is not amused on how everyone treats him like the "fifth wheel".

characters.name: Daphne Blake
characters.description: Took a Level in Badass: Tired of being theDamsel in Distress, Daphne pumps herself with steroids to turn into a super, hulking brute.

characters.name: Velma Dinkley
characters.description: Disney Villain Death: Falls from a really tall building but she still lives, other than suffering a major spine injury. Sole Survivor: Is the only one left alive in "Scooby Friday" afterJason Vorheesmurdered the rest of Mystery Inc.

characters.name: Archie Andrews
characters.description: And I Must Scream: Sent to Hell to "scream and cry" for aiding Veronica in the murder spree. Extreme Doormat: Winds up in Veronica's toxic influence and becomes her partner in her heinous actions. They Killed Kenny Again: He dies a lot throughout the special. Unwitting Instigator of Doom: Archie accidentally mouths off to Polly (Bitch Pudding) that the football team has beenSlut-ShamingBetty resulting in a massacre on the entire team.

characters.name: Betty Cooper
characters.description: Morality Pet: Despite their strained relationship, Polly (Bitch Pudding) loves Betty dearly and Betty is touched that her older sister slaughtered the entire football team forSlut-Shamingher.

characters.name: Veronica Lodge
characters.description: Asshole Victim: She's unarguably the least sympathetic out of between herself and Archie; she is a toxic influence towards Archie, tried to steal her family's money to elope with him, killing her father then everyone else because she can. No tears are shed for her when Moose shoots her and Archie dead. Evil Laugh: After killing her father, Veronica, according to Archie, laughed like a demon that sent a chill on his spine. Noodle Incident: For some reason, Veronica developed hemorrhoids after swallowing a ton of diamonds. OOC Is Serious Business: This version of Veronica is an exaggerated take on theRich Bitch, going to borderline villain at times, but the fact she acts meek around Polly Cooper (Bitch Pudding) makes it clear that not even she wants to mess around Betty's psychotic older sister. Screw the Rules, I Have Money!: She offers Death a million dollars to spare her. It works.

characters.name: Jughead Jones
characters.description: Undignified Death: While he is taking a shower, Jughead vomits and tries to flush them all in, only to slip and fall right into his surprisingly sharp hat. The news doesn't try to hide how stupid the death is.Stupid Kid impaled on Stupid Hat.

characters.name: Reggie Mantle
characters.description: Ain't Too Proud to Beg: When Veronica and Archie come for him, Reggie got down on his knees and beg. They shoot him.Archie:Not even killing Reggie made us feel fulfilled. Be Careful What You Wish For: Reggie tries to stave off Polly's (Bitch Pudding) wrath that he has to be the antagonist to make life interesting. Polly agrees because how else can she justify insmashing Reggie's dickwith a locker. Too Dumb to Live: Tries to get close to the obviously voracious Bleeps to record a video to his account.

characters.name: Mario
characters.description: Big Brother Instinct: Mario would make sure you'll burn in Hell if you so much harm his brother, Luigi. Diet Episode: He, along with the other fat characters attend the Fattest Fat Loser Competition to lose some pounds. The end result is him becoming even more obese after devouring a roasted Miss Piggy. Get-Rich-Quick Scheme: Mario uses the Coin Blocks to produce endless amount of gold coins to get rich. It didn't take long before his overspending causes him to lose it all.

characters.name: Yoshi
characters.description: Devoured by the Horde: After stumbling into Racoon City, he immediately gets jumped on by zombies and devoured. The Dog Bites Back: Kills Mario and Luigi for mistreating him.

characters.name: Papa Smurf
characters.description: Bad Boss: Papa Smurf treats the other Smurfs like low-paid employees. I Ate WHAT?!: Papa Smurf goes green after learning he has been drinking caterpillar milk for years. King Incognito: Happens in "Undercover Smurf Boss" where Papa Smurf sees what's happening within the day-to-day operations in the village.

characters.name: Brainy Smurf
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: Becomes the focal character in "Murder in Smurf Town X" and "House of Smurfs". Graceful Loser:Brainy Smurf is totally fine with Hefy Smurf becoming second-in-command, agreeing with everyone that he is hot. Rage Breaking Point: After being kicked out once again by the other Smurfs, Brainy Smurf decides enough is enough and forms a Machiavellian scheme to win over the second-in-command position. Villain Protagonist: In "House of Smurfs", Brainy Smurf concocts a scheme to eliminate the competition and become second-in-command.

characters.name: Jokey Smurf
characters.description: Ax-Crazy:Jokey becomes a mass-murdering psycho that is killing the various Smurfs. Die Laughing:Subverted. Jokey doesn't laugh after having spear shot right through him. Theme Serial Killer:Being inspired by John Doe fromSe7en, Jokey's M.O. are styled theSeven Deadly Sins.

characters.name: Handy Smurf
characters.description: Blackmail: He is forced to help Brainy Smurf in his plot under threat of revealing to the village that he used to do hand jobs. Fingore: Loses his fingers in an incident where he has to saw through a mushroom. He Knows Too Much: Papa Smurf tried to have Handy assassinated to keep him from learning the truth of him eliminating the outdated Smurfs. Handy overcomes the assassin and confronts Papa Smurf.

characters.name: Gargamel
characters.description: Bad People Abuse Animals: Gargamel haskicked Azaraelon multiple occasions and forgot to feed him once. Becoming the Mask: Gargamel transfers his mind into a Smurf and lives with them until he finds true happiness thanks to his interactions with the Smurfs. Fan Disservice: No one should experience thehorrorof a Smurf Burger commercial, featuring Gargamel in a bikini and a close-up of his mouth eating the burger. Team Rocket Wins: Gargamel has been successfully able to eat the Smurfs here far more than the original show.

characters.name: E.T.
characters.description: Flipping the Bird: E.T. does this with his glowing finger. Given Name Reveal: The other aliens reveal that E.T.'s name is Kleborp. No Respect for the Village Idiot: E.T. is actually the planet's retard and his fellow aliens left him there because they didn't want him. Super Doc: E.T. was meant to be this onStevenSpielberg's failed pitch, "E.T. Emergency Terrestrial. Ungrateful Bastard: In "E.T. Alternative Ending'', E.T. has Elliot and the other humans who helped him killed to cover his race's existence.E.T.:No Witnesses.

characters.name: Willy Wonka
characters.description: Manipulative Bastard: Leaves Charlie to becomeThe Scapegoatof murdering the other children.

characters.name: Dorothy
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Dorothy's actual father sexually abused her and she is horrified that she accidentally returned home and to him. Death by Irony: After unknowingly causing the death of the Wicked Witch of the East by dropping a house onto her, Dorothy is killed by another house owned byCarl Fredricksen. Promoted to Love Interest: In "The Wizard of Vomit", it's revealed that Dorothy is sexually intimate with Scarecrow, as her vomiting straw implies she fellated him offscreen.

characters.name: Tin Man
characters.description: Defeated and Trophified: The Tin Man was thrown into a compressor and turned into a cube which the Wizard used as a footstool. Driven to Suicide: Tin Man can't take the pressure of being in prison, so he ties a noose around his neck and ends himself.

characters.name: Cowardly Lion
characters.description: Defeated and Trophified: The Wizard had the lion skinned and be used as a rug on his floor.

characters.name: Bruce
characters.description: Berserk Button: Never call the shark fat. The Can Kicked Him: Bruce attacks a woman resembling Chrissie Watkins from the toilet when she was shatting on it. Why Don't You Just Shoot Him?: After getting triggered by Brody's "We're gonna need a bigger boat" line, Bruce takes out a rifle and shoot him and the crew.

characters.name: Barbie
characters.description: The Diss Track: Barbie unloads one onto a rival rapper for making fun of her resume and status. Drill Sergeant Nasty: She constantly pushes the contestants in "The Fattest Fat Loser" competition. Look Both Ways: Gets run over by theBratz's car.

characters.name: Count von Count
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: In "Seasame Street Meets Blade", the Count converts most of the Sesame Streeters into vampires thenBladearrives to deal with them. Bring Me My Brown Pants: The Count crap himself when Blade is going to kill him. Feed It a Bomb:Bladeshoves a grenade right down through the Count's mouth.

characters.name: Grover
characters.description: Cruel and Unusual Death: Grover dies when a lightning strikes on the metal helmet. No-Holds-Barred Beatdown: When Super Grover arrives to save the day,Doomsdayappears to give the hero the beatdown of the life time.

characters.name: Oscar the Grouch
characters.description: Didn't Think This Through: Vampire Oscar thinksBladecan't penetrate his trash can, only for the vampire hunter to just open the lid and fire on the occupant.

characters.name: Big Bird
characters.description: Off with His Head!:Bladecuts his head off.

characters.name: Indiana Jones
characters.description: Everyone Has Standards: Indy would rather just across than grabbing onto Satipo's dick. You Killed My Father: Indiana Jones' fear of snakes stems from his snake stepfather not only attacking his father but alsoswallowing his mother whole.

characters.name: Satipo
characters.description: Adaptational Heroism: Satipo did try to help Indy but has the man try to swing across by grabbing onto his dick. Gag Penis: The dick is so long it can be used as a rope.

characters.name: SpongeBobSquarePants
characters.description: Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: While Sandy is shown to be nothing more than friends withSpongeBobin the original series, one sketch depicts the two as a couple, whereSpongeBobasks Sandy how she can be pregnant when she said she had a sponge inside of her. Then he realizes that she was talking about him. Captain Ersatz: The season 1 episode "That Hurts Me" has lawyer-friendly clones of him and Patrick, withSpongeBobhaving black arms and legs, a button-like nose, an abrasive pad on his back, and no clothing aside from having sneakers rather than black shoes. Freak Out:SpongeBobloses his mind when he discovers what Krabby Patties are made of in the "Krabby Patties" sketch.

characters.name: Eugene H. Krabs
characters.description: Adaptational Villainy: While Mr. Krabs was certainly far from a great boss in the canon series, here he is depicted as being a full-blown psychopath who may be more evil than Plankton, asSpongeBobreveals that he's been killing fish (and his own kind) and feeding them to the customers at the Krusty Krab. You Bastard!: Mr. Krabs callsSpongeBoba "little yellow bastard" when he reveals his true nature in the "Krabby Patties" sketch.

characters.name: Sheriff Woody
characters.description: Mercy Kill: Is forced to kill Buzz in order to put him out of his misery in the "Toy Story 4" sketch. Oh, Crap!: In "Toy Story 4", when Andy states that he left his favourite toy at college, Woody realizes that he's no longer Andy's favourite toy and is horrified to find out what his new favourite is. Tears from a Stone: Sheds tears after killing Buzz despite being a toy. Vorpal Pillow: After Buzz gets lobotomized, Woody smothers him with a pillow to end his suffering.

characters.name: Buzz Lightyear
characters.description: Cruel and Unusual Death: In "Toy Story 4", Buzz gets his helmet and his head smashed open, a nozzle shoved into his groins, and is used to smoke pot, which effectively lobotomizes him. After that, Woody suffocates him by smothering him with a pillow, sealing his doom. Death by Adaptation: Buzz dies in the "Toy Story 4" sketch. Groin Attack: Buzz gets a nozzle shoved between his legs in "Toy Story 4". Lobotomy: In "Toy Story 4", Andy realizes that he left his bong at college, so he decides to "improvise" by turning Buzz into a bong. After getting his head cut open and being used to smoke pot, Buzz is left with zero brain cells and is reduced to a blathering idiot as a result. Simpleton Voice: Buzz speaks with a silly, childlike voice after being lobotomized in the "Toy Story 4" sketch.

characters.name: Seth Green
characters.description: The show's egotistical creator. Adam Westing: Seth plays himself, with a massively inflated ego. Boom, Headshot!: He is shot in the head.More than once. Rousing Speech: Gives one to the recurring characters in "Beginning Season Five". Set Right What Once Went Wrong: After the show gets cancelled for the first time, he has the chance to go back in time and undo the event that caused it (a bucket ofgreenpaint falling overKeith Crofford).

characters.name: Matthew Senreich
characters.description: The show's second banana to Seth, and moderately more sane. Adam Westing: Plays a ditzy, psychotic version of himself. Ax-Crazy: At least two season finales have ended with him killing everyone. Bad Acting: Let's say... he's a better writer than voice actor. The Ditz: Occasionally. He goes on a shooting rampage in the Telethon when he was supposed to only shoot the puppy if nobody called. And he goes "Wow!" when reading it on his cellphone screen before realizing it's upside down and it actually reads "Mom".

characters.name: Doug Goldstein
characters.description: The shows co-head writer. Gets possibly even less respect than Matt. Insistent Terminology: Always introduced as "Co-head writer Doug Goldstein".

characters.name: Mike Lazzo
characters.description: The all-powerful head honcho of[adult swim], always ready to cancel the show. Big Bad: In almost any meta sketch, as he is shown either canceling the show or in favor of it. Biting-the-Hand Humor: Not giving a very favorable portrayal otherwise, either. Groin Attack: In "A Very Dragon Ball Z Christmas", he is kicked multiple times there by the Nutcracker. Hidden Depths: He is shown dancing to many different tunes at the end of Season 4.

characters.name: Keith Crofford
characters.description: The executive vicepresident of [adult swim]. Beleaguered Assistant: Implied in the sketch where he renews the show without consulting Lazzo, who is clearly not happy about it. However, he is not free of quirkiness himself. Biting-the-Hand Humor: Same deal with Lazzo. Mutual Kill: ...only to hit Lazzo while he sinks his machete on Crofford's back. However, the Chicken kills them first... Off with His Head!: ...by stomping their heads together.

characters.name: Joey Fatone
characters.description: A former member of*NSYNC. You know, the fat one. All Your Powers Combined: Joey harnesses the powers of the other *NSYNC to grow to theBritneyAbomination's size and fight her. And Zoidberg: TheYakuzassent to murder the *NSYNC don't even recognize him as a member of the group. The Cameo: Has one in the firstStar Warsspecial as part of the Max Rebo's Greatest Hits sketch, doing a duet with the titular musician called "Neither Of Us Is An Elephant." Continuity Nod: He will appear sometimes wearing the karate costume from "Enter the Fat One", despite no reference made to karate.

characters.name: Lindsay Lohan
characters.description: A rather unflattering portrayal ofthe disgraced child actress. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Calls Munson a bad boy and falls instantly in love with him. And Zoidberg: When she's revealed to be part of theVinvasion troops, she's trusted to...carry a cup of coffee.Which she immediately drops. She's then told to do anything she wants. Batman Can Breathe in Space: She flies through space without a suit at the end of "There can be only one Lohan" (a.k.a.Highlohander). Bulletproof Human Shield: Acts as an involuntary one for the Gummy Bear in "Beginning Season Five".

characters.name: Britney Spears
characters.description: The former teen pop star, and person whom Seth Green presumably hated the most before transferring his sights to Lohan. All Your Powers Combined: In "Enter the Fat One", she fuses herself withChristina Aguilera,Avril Lavigne,Jessica SimpsonandAshlee Simpsonto become the giantKaiju-like"Britney Abomination" and kill him. And Zoidberg: She doesn't consider Ashlee Simpson worthy of any introduction besides "Jessica Simpson's Sister" and tells her to shut up because "adults are talking". Body Horror: Her fusion with other pop stars and transformation into the giant and aptly named "Britney Abomination", which has a head in place of each hand and foot. Buried Alive: At the end of "Enter the Fat One".

characters.name: George W. Bush
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: The President is not really sound of mind given the number of shenanigans he gets himself into. Drunk with Power: After somehow having the ability to use the Force, it doesn't take long for Bush to abuse the heck out of it.
